title: Runtime rollout automation for private data plane: zero-downtime + safe rollback
creator: Aria Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood Private customers require the ability to apply runtime/data-plane upgrades (runtime binary, inference engine patch, or model runtime config) with zero or near-zero downtime. Current manual procedures are slow and error-prone: cluster drain, manual KV warm-up, manual traffic shift, and manual rollback. This ticket scopes automation that uses our IaC modules (Terraform), orchestration hooks, and health-checks to perform staged rollouts with automatic rollback triggers for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.

Goal:
Create an automated, documented, and testable rollout pipeline for data-plane/runtime upgrades that supports canary -> progressive -> full rollout, enforces health gates, gracefully drains connections, preserves KV cache where possible, and can automatically rollback on predefined failure signals. The automation must be usable by customers via our Terraform modules and by SRE for on-prem upgrades.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A Terraform-driven pipeline (module inputs + example) that can trigger a canary upgrade to 5% of nodes in a VPC/private deployment and then progress to 25% and 100% according to health gates.
2) Health gates include: readiness probes, inference tail-latency (p95/p99 thresholds), error-rate increase > 2x baseline, failed streaming sessions > 1% over 5 minutes, and KV-cache warmup success for canary nodes.
3) Zero client-visible dropped requests during normal traffic profiles and documented graceful connection draining for in-flight requests.
4) Automatic rollback occurs if any gate fails and the system restores previous runtime on failed nodes within the pipeline window.
5) Runbook and a one-click manual abort + rollback CLI for SRE; Confluence runbook linked in ticket.
6) Integration tests (CI) that simulate canary failure and validate automatic rollback to baseline.
7) Security review completed and Terraform changes pass static-scan.
proposed_solution:
High level:
- Extend private Terraform modules with a 'rollout' resource that emits rollout objects (metadata, target node selectors, new runtime image/version, rollout strategy).
- Implement an orchestration controller (stateless controller run in control plane) that watches rollout objects and coordinates per-node upgrade steps through the existing agent RPC.
- Rollout strategy: canary -> linear progressive (5%, 25%, 100%). Pause window between stages.
- Per-node upgrade steps: preflight compatibility check (model+kernel), schedule agent to pull new runtime, start new runtime alongside old on same host where resource allows (side-by-side), warm KV cache and kernel caches, health-check warmup probes, shift small percentage of traffic via network proxy / service mesh, monitor gates, then drain old process and remove.
- Rollback strategy: if any gate fails, the controller signals agents to revert to saved previous runtime snapshot and re-route traffic back to healthy nodes.
- Expose hooks in Terraform module to configure thresholds and fallback behavior.
- Provide opt-in 'hosted-fallback' toggle to route traffic to Redwood hosted endpoints for high-severity failures (enterprise customers only, and only when policy allows).
rollout_plan:
1) Spike (2 days): prototype controller logic and proof-of-concept that performs a canary on a dev private cluster using scripted steps.
2) Module update (3 days): add rollout resource schema and example usage to Terraform module.
3) Controller + agent RPC (7 days): implement safe upgrade handshake, preflight checks, and KV warmup signal.
4) Health gates + metrics (3 days): wire p95/p99 and error-rate monitors, define thresholds, add automatic rollback trigger.
5) CI tests & chaos (3 days): simulate failures in CI, test rollback.
6) Security review & docs (2 days): finish review, publish runbook.
7) Pilot with 2 enterprise customers (2 weeks): coordinate scheduled upgrade windows.
Total estimated: ~20 working days (spread across 2 sprints).
health_checks:
- readiness probe: /internal/healthy and runtime-specific readiness.
- warmup_metric: kv_cache_entries_count >= baseline * 0.85 within 3 minutes.
- latency_metrics: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.1, p99 <= baseline_p99 * 1.25.
- error_rate: 5xx / total_requests increase <= 2x baseline over 5m window.
- streaming_session_loss: <= 1% loss over 5m.
- memory_rss: no OOMs or >90% memory usage.
- kernel_compatibility: agent returns code 0 from preflight check.
- business-aligned smoke tests: run the canonical eval prompt set for 30s on canary nodes and assert intent-level similarity within configured tolerance.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Rollout dashboard: per-rollout progress, nodes upgraded, gate pass/fail, time-in-stage.
- Alerts: Rollout-stage-Failure (pagerduty), AutoRollbackTriggered (pagerduty-high), Rollout-Stuck (>15 minutes in stage without progress).
- Annotate traces with rollout_id for request-level analysis.
- Cost metric: additional memory/CPU when running side-by-side binaries to detect oversubscription.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for controller state machine.
- Integration test in private-dev cluster: run full canary->failure->rollback cycle.
- Chaos run: randomly kill canary node during warmup to validate controller tolerances.
- Performance validation: ensure no request loss under normal traffic (use replay tool with recorded production traffic samples).
- Security tests: terraform static checks, secrets handling for agent RPC, RBAC checks for rollout API.
